title: Lesson 3 — Recording Business Transactions
summary: BBM140 Week 1 Tutorial — the extended accounting equation, recording transactions in a worksheet, preparing the balance sheet and income statement, profit retention, and double-entry bookkeeping (journal and T-accounts).

blocks.title: 🎯 Learning objectives
items: Extend the accounting equation to include capital, revenues and expenses.
Record business transactions in a worksheet, keeping the equation in balance.
Prepare a simple balance sheet and income statement from the worksheet.
Explain profit retention and the link between the income statement and balance sheet.
Apply the debit/credit rules and record transactions as journal entries and T-accounts.

blocks.title: 1. The fundamental equation revisited
blocks.content:
Start from the accounting equation and expand **equity** into its parts:

$$\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity}$$

Equity contains the owners' capital **plus profit**:

$$\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + [\,\text{Capital \& Other Equity} + \text{Profit}\,]$$

and profit itself is **revenues minus expenses**:

$$\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + [\,\text{Capital \& Other Equity} + (\text{Revenues} - \text{Expenses})\,]$$

Because the equation always holds, it also holds for **changes** (Δ):

$$\Delta \text{Assets} = \Delta \text{Liabilities} + \Delta[\,\text{Capital \& Other Equity} + \text{Revenues} - \text{Expenses}\,]$$

> **Key idea:** this relation is true for *each individual transaction*. Every transaction keeps the equation in balance.

blocks.title: 2. The worksheet — Paul & Mary's HotPizza
blocks.content:
We record transactions in a **worksheet** with one column per account, grouped as **Assets = Liabilities + Equity**:

| | Fixed Assets | Stock | Cash & Bank | Accounts Payable | Share Capital | Retained Profit | Profit (I/S) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Each transaction is written as one or more **+/−** entries across the columns, always keeping **Assets = Liabilities + Equity**.

**The six transactions of Paul & Mary's HotPizza restaurant:**
1. Paul and Mary deposit **£1,000** in a bank account to start the business.
2. Purchase of **£250** cash of goods for stock.
3. Purchase of restaurant equipment **on credit** for **£300**.
4. Payment of **80%** of the equipment bill.
5. Sale of pizzas for **£150** cash which **cost £100**.
6. Weekly salaries of **£30** paid to Paul and Mary.

blocks.title: 3. Recording each transaction (the Δ view)
blocks.content:
**T1 — Deposit £1,000 to start the business**
$$+1000\ (\text{Bank}) = +1000\ (\text{Share capital})$$

**T2 — Buy £250 of goods for cash**
$$+250\ (\text{Inventory}),\ -250\ (\text{Bank})$$
*An asset swap: one asset (cash) is exchanged for another (inventory).*

**T3 — Buy equipment on credit, £300**
$$+300\ (\text{Fixed assets}) = +300\ (\text{Accounts payable})$$

**T4 — Pay 80% of the equipment bill (£240)**
$$-240\ (\text{Bank}) = -240\ (\text{Accounts payable})$$
*Part of the liability disappears from the balance sheet.*

**T5 — Sell pizzas for £150 cash that cost £100**
$$+150\ (\text{Bank}),\ -100\ (\text{Inventory}) = +50\ (\text{Profit})$$
*In the income statement: Sales 150 − Cost of sales 100 = Profit 50.*

**T6 — Pay £30 weekly salaries**
$$-30\ (\text{Bank}) = -30\ (\text{Profit})$$
*In the income statement: Salaries expense (30), reducing profit.*

blocks.title: 4. The completed worksheet
blocks.content:
| Transaction | Fixed Assets | Stock | Cash & Bank | = | Accounts Payable | + | Share Capital | Retained Profit | Profit (I/S) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|:-:|---:|:-:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 Initial capital | | | +1000 | | | | +1000 | | |
| 2 Purchase pizzas | | +250 | −250 | | | | | | |
| 3 Purchase equipment | +300 | | | | +300 | | | | |
| 4 Payment equipment | | | −240 | | −240 | | | | |
| 5 Sales pizzas | | | +150 | | | | | | +150 |
| 5 Cost of sales | | −100 | | | | | | | −100 |
| 6 Salaries | | | −30 | | | | | | −30 |
| **Closing balances** | **300** | **150** | **630** | | **60** | | **1000** | | **+20** |

Use the columns to build the statements:
- the **Profit (I/S)** column → the **income statement**,
- the **Cash & Bank** column → the **cash flow statement**,
- the **closing balances** row → the **balance sheet**.

blocks.title: 🧪 Try it yourself — build the HotPizza worksheet
blocks.prompt: Run the worksheet engine below. It applies each transaction as a set of +/− entries and checks that **Assets = Liabilities + Equity** after every step. Then try adding a transaction of your own.
blocks.starter:
accounts = {
    "Fixed assets": 0, "Stock": 0, "Cash & bank": 0,   # assets
    "Accounts payable": 0,                                # liabilities
    "Share capital": 0, "Profit": 0,                      # equity
}
ASSETS      = ["Fixed assets", "Stock", "Cash & bank"]
LIABILITIES = ["Accounts payable"]
EQUITY      = ["Share capital", "Profit"]

def post(label, **entries):
    for acc, amt in entries.items():
        accounts[acc] += amt
    a = sum(accounts[k] for k in ASSETS)
    l = sum(accounts[k] for k in LIABILITIES)
    e = sum(accounts[k] for k in EQUITY)
    ok = "OK" if abs(a - (l + e)) < 1e-9 else "!! OUT OF BALANCE"
    print(f"{label:22s} A={a:7.0f}  L={l:5.0f}  E={e:6.0f}   {ok}")

post("1 Deposit capital", **{"Cash & bank": +1000, "Share capital": +1000})
post("2 Buy stock (cash)", **{"Stock": +250, "Cash & bank": -250})
post("3 Buy equip (credit)", **{"Fixed assets": +300, "Accounts payable": +300})
post("4 Pay 80% of bill", **{"Cash & bank": -240, "Accounts payable": -240})
post("5 Sell pizzas", **{"Cash & bank": +150, "Stock": -100, "Profit": +50})
post("6 Pay salaries", **{"Cash & bank": -30, "Profit": -30})

print("\nClosing balances:")
for k, v in accounts.items():
    print(f"  {k:18s} {v:7.0f}")

blocks.title: 5. Profit retention — linking I/S and B/S
blocks.content:
At period end, profit is **transferred** out of the temporary *Profit for the year* account (an income-statement account) and **retained** inside equity, in the **Retained profit** account:

| Equity | |
|---|---:|
| Retained profit | **+20** |
| Profit for the year | **−20** |

The income statement is 'emptied' into retained earnings. The general link is:

$$\text{Ending retained profit} = \text{Beginning retained profit} + \text{Net profit} - \text{Dividends}$$

For HotPizza (no opening balance, no dividend): ending retained profit = 0 + 20 − 0 = **£20**.

blocks.title: 6. The resulting statements
blocks.content:
**Income statement at the end of the period**

| | Amount (£) |
|---|---:|
| Revenues | 150 |
| Cost of sales | (100) |
| Salaries | (30) |
| **Profit for the year** | **20** |

**Balance sheet at the end of the period**

| Assets | £ | Liabilities & Equity | £ |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Cash & Bank | 630 | Accounts payable | 60 |
| Inventory | 150 | Equity | 1,020 |
| Fixed Assets | 300 | | |
| **Total Assets** | **1,080** | **Total L + E** | **1,080** |

Equity 1,020 = share capital 1,000 + retained profit 20. The balance sheet **balances**. ✔

blocks.title: 7. Double-entry bookkeeping — debit/credit rules
blocks.content:
Instead of a worksheet, accountants traditionally use **double-entry bookkeeping**: every transaction has **two effects** — a **debit** and an equal **credit**. From the fundamental equation:

| | Assets | Liabilities | Equity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Increase ↑** | **Debit** | Credit | Credit |
| **Decrease ↓** | Credit | **Debit** | **Debit** |

Rearranging the extended equation to put all 'debit-natured' items on one side:

$$\text{Assets} + \text{Expense} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Share Capital} + \text{Revenue}$$

| | Assets / **Expense** | Liabilities | Equity / **Revenue** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Increase ↑** | **Debit** | Credit | Credit |
| **Decrease ↓** | Credit | **Debit** | **Debit** |

So an **expense** increase is a **debit**; a **revenue** increase is a **credit**. For every entry: **total debits = total credits**.

blocks.title: 8. The journal — HotPizza
blocks.content:
Recording the six transactions as journal entries (Dr = debit, Cr = credit):

| # | Entry | Dr | Cr |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Dr Cash & Banks / Cr Share capital | 1000 | 1000 |
| 2 | Dr Inventory (purchase) / Cr Cash & Banks | 250 | 250 |
| 3 | Dr Fixed assets / Cr Accounts payable | 300 | 300 |
| 4 | Dr Accounts payable / Cr Cash & Banks | 240 | 240 |
| 5 | Dr Cash & Banks / Cr Sales revenue (I/S) | 150 | 150 |
| 5 | Dr Cost of sales (I/S) / Cr Stock | 100 | 100 |
| 6 | Dr Salaries expense (I/S) / Cr Cash & Banks | 30 | 30 |

Notice each line has equal debit and credit.

blocks.title: 9. T-accounts
blocks.content:
Another way to do bookkeeping is with **T-accounts** — one 'T' per account, **debit on the left, credit on the right**:

```
        Account
   ----------------
   Debit  |  Credit
   (left) |  (right)
```

**The rules by account type:**

| Account type | Increase | Decrease |
|---|---|---|
| **Assets** | Debit (left) | Credit (right) |
| **Liabilities** | Credit (right) | Debit (left) |
| **Owners' equity** | Credit (right) | Debit (left) |
| **Expenses** (↓ equity) | Debit (left) | Credit (right) |
| **Revenues** (↑ equity) | Credit (right) | Debit (left) |

Revenues and expenses are **temporary** T-accounts: they collect changes in retained earnings during the period, and at period end their balances are **transferred to retained earnings**.

**Example — transactions 1, 2 and 3:**

```
  Cash & Banks (A)          Share Capital (E)
  [1] 1,000 | [2] 250                 | [1] 1,000

  Inventory (A)             Fixed assets (A)
  [2]   250 |               [3]   300 |

  Acc. Payable (L)
            | [3] 300
```

**Total debits (1,550) = Total credits (1,550).** ✔

blocks.title: 🧪 Try it yourself — check debits = credits
blocks.prompt: A trial balance works only if total debits equal total credits. Run the HotPizza journal below; the engine posts each Dr/Cr pair and verifies the books balance.
blocks.starter:
journal = [
    ("Cash & Banks",     "Share capital",    1000),
    ("Inventory",        "Cash & Banks",      250),
    ("Fixed assets",     "Accounts payable",  300),
    ("Accounts payable", "Cash & Banks",      240),
    ("Cash & Banks",     "Sales revenue",     150),
    ("Cost of sales",    "Stock",             100),
    ("Salaries expense", "Cash & Banks",       30),
]

total_dr = total_cr = 0
print(f"{'Dr account':18s}{'Cr account':18s}{'Amount':>8s}")
for dr, cr, amt in journal:
    total_dr += amt
    total_cr += amt
    print(f"{dr:18s}{cr:18s}{amt:8.0f}")

print("-" * 44)
print(f"Total debits = {total_dr}, total credits = {total_cr}")
print("Balanced!" if total_dr == total_cr else "NOT balanced")

items.definition: Assets = Liabilities + [Capital & Other Equity + (Revenues − Expenses)]. Holds for every transaction and for changes (Δ).
A table with one column per account (grouped A = L + E) used to record each transaction as +/− entries while keeping the equation in balance.
A transaction that exchanges one asset for another (e.g. cash → inventory); total assets, liabilities and equity are unchanged.
The cost of the inventory that was sold; recorded as an expense that reduces profit when a sale is made.
Transferring profit for the year from the income statement into retained profit (within equity) at period end.
Ending retained profit = Beginning retained profit + Net profit − Dividends.
Each transaction is recorded with equal debits and credits, so total debits always equal total credits.
Assets & expenses increase with a debit; liabilities, equity & revenues increase with a credit.
A chronological list of transactions written as debit/credit entries.
A single account shown as a 'T': debits on the left, credits on the right; one per asset, liability, equity, revenue and expense.

cards.front: Expand equity in the accounting equation.
Sell goods for £150 cash that cost £100 — the effect?
cards.back: +150 cash, −100 inventory, +50 profit (Sales 150 − Cost of sales 100).
Exchanging one asset for another (e.g. cash for inventory); the equation is unchanged.
Transferring profit for the year into retained profit within equity at period end.
Beginning retained profit + Net profit − Dividends.

cards.front: Debit/credit: assets and expenses increase with a…?
cards.back: Debit. (Liabilities, equity and revenues increase with a credit.)

cards.front: In a T-account, which side is debit?
cards.back: The left side (credit on the right).

cards.front: Why are revenues and expenses 'temporary' accounts?
cards.back: They collect period changes in retained earnings and are closed to retained earnings at period end.

questions.q: Buying £250 of inventory for cash is an example of:
questions.explanation: One asset (cash) decreases and another (inventory) increases by the same amount — an asset swap. Totals are unchanged.

questions.q: Selling goods for £150 that cost £100 changes profit by:
questions.explanation: Revenue +150 and cost of sales −100 give a profit of +50.

options: Reduces cash and reduces accounts payable by 240
Reduces cash and reduces equity by 240
Has no effect on the balance sheet
questions.explanation: −240 cash (asset) and −240 accounts payable (liability): part of the liability is settled.

questions.q: Under the debit/credit rules, an increase in an expense is a:
questions.explanation: Expenses increase with a debit (like assets); revenues increase with a credit (like equity).

questions.q: At period end, profit retention means:
options: Paying out profit as a dividend
Transferring profit for the year into retained profit within equity
Moving cash into a reserve account
questions.explanation: Profit for the year (a temporary I/S account) is transferred into retained profit inside equity.

questions.q: In a T-account for a LIABILITY, an increase is recorded on the:
questions.explanation: Liabilities (and equity and revenues) increase on the credit (right) side; assets and expenses increase on the debit (left).

blocks.title: 📝 Recap
blocks.content: Expanding equity gives the extended equation Assets = Liabilities + [Capital + (Revenues − Expenses)], which holds for every transaction. Using a worksheet, we recorded Paul & Mary's HotPizza transactions as +/− entries that always keep the books in balance, then read the income statement off the profit column and the balance sheet off the closing-balance row. Profit for the year is retained into equity at period end (ending retained profit = beginning + net profit − dividends), linking the two statements. The same transactions can be captured with double-entry bookkeeping — equal debits and credits — recorded as journal entries or T-accounts, where assets and expenses increase with a debit and liabilities, equity and revenues increase with a credit, so total debits always equal total credits.
